- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. {"id":"SMA-580","title":"Release activation E: pre-flight checklist + flip PAIGASUS_RELEASE_ENABLED","description":"Final increment of <issue id="d81426f7-9563-4632-ad1b-b5dd4d0b57c4" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-407/release-activation-000-010-floor-kernelproto-lockstep-wiring-live">SMA-407</issue>, per §10 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-sma-407-release-activation-design.md`. Blocked on <issue id="58a95803-beac-456d-90da-1b13eec12279" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-576/release-activation-a-kernel-family-010-floor-repoversion-lockstep-gate">SMA-576</issue>, <issue id="46b1513e-1fb2-4883-a327-9ce7845bd614" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-577/release-activation-b-make-the-proto-family-publishable-absorbs-sma-388">SMA-577</issue>, <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue>, <issue id="de922f9c-1e93-4869-a2aa-c2e1ad2446dd" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-579/release-activation-d-npm-activation-napirelease-plz-tagging-boundary">SMA-579</issue>.

The single irreversible step. Everything before this is reversible; this is not.

## Pre-flight checklist — all of it, before flipping

- [ ] `paigasus-kernel`, `paigasus-proto`, `paigasus-proto-derive` free on [crates.io](<http://crates.io>)
- [ ] `paigasus-kernel`, `paigasus-proto`, `paigasus-py-bindings` free on PyPI
- [ ] the `@paigasus` npm scope owned by this project
- [ ] **no workspace member name squatted on [crates.io](<http://crates.io>)** — with `git_only` unset, release-plz performs a registry lookup for *every* member name (`paigasus-logging`, `paigasus-observability`, …), so a squatted name would silently become the version-comparison baseline
- [ ] the repository is **public** — `docs/ops/RUNBOOK-go-public.md` documents a flip not yet executed, so every published `repository` / `homepage` URL currently 404s
- [ ] `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` **repository secret exists**, issued from the **existing Paigasus bot GitHub App** (reuse it — do not create a second App). It needs `contents: write` + `pull-requests: write` on this repo.
  **Why not the default** `GITHUB_TOKEN`**:** GitHub does not trigger `pull_request` workflows for a PR opened by it, so `moon ci` — the required check on the `Protect main` ruleset — would never run and the release PR could never be merged.
  **Needed earlier than the rest of this checklist.** The `release-pr` job shipped live in <issue id="58a95803-beac-456d-90da-1b13eec12279" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-576/release-activation-a-kernel-family-010-floor-repoversion-lockstep-gate">SMA-576</issue>, and its preflight step makes the whole job **skip cleanly (green)** while the secret is absent. That is deliberate (an unguarded job would have reddened `main` on every push), but it means the release path is silently inert until this is done, with nothing in CI to say so. Create it as soon as <issue id="58a95803-beac-456d-90da-1b13eec12279" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-576/release-activation-a-kernel-family-010-floor-repoversion-lockstep-gate">SMA-576</issue> merges if you want to observe the job at all — the item below depends on it.
- [ ] the `release-pr` job has been observed proposing sane versions on real merges

## Expected first-release behaviour

release-plz's baseline is the [**crates.io**](<http://crates.io>) **registry**, not git tags — `ci/release-parity/ecosystems/release-plz.sh:43` sets `git_only = true` precisely to *avoid* the registry lookup for fixture crates, and `rs/release-plz.toml` sets no `git_only`. For a package absent from the registry, the expected behaviour is to treat it as new and propose the **manifest version** — `0.1.0`, no bump.

So the likely observation is an **empty release PR**, not an over-bump. Decide what acceptance evidence looks like in that case.

## Never

Do not hand-place a `*-vX.Y.Z` tag to seed release-plz's tracking. Manual tags lack the metadata release-plz uses to track releases and silently stop all future bumps — the <issue id="4900dca8-16c8-4891-8156-3de7c54b6e90" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-385/release-plz-isnt-bumping-paigasus-helikon-core-past-010-on-featcore">SMA-385</issue> failure, and the direct motivation for ADR-0011 S3's "the tool owns every tag".

## Rollback reality

[crates.io](<http://crates.io>) supports only `cargo yank` (never delete, never reuse); PyPI supports delete-but-never-reuse; npm supports unpublish within 72 hours only. A wrong publish is a permanent version burn in two of three registries.

## Also here

The ADR-0011 amendment (spec §13), if not already landed with <issue id="58a95803-beac-456d-90da-1b13eec12279" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-576/release-activation-a-kernel-family-010-floor-repoversion-lockstep-gate">SMA-576</issue>.

## Also: a one-line comment fix in release.yml

`.github/workflows/release.yml`'s Checkout step explains *why* an App token is required but does not say **which** App. Add that it reuses the **existing Paigasus bot GitHub App** — so nobody creates a second one while debugging why the job skips.

Not done in <issue id="58a95803-beac-456d-90da-1b13eec12279" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-576/release-activation-a-kernel-family-010-floor-repoversion-lockstep-gate">SMA-576</issue>: it surfaced after CI was already mid-flight on the final commit, and restarting the full matrix (7 prebuild legs + images + `moon ci`) for a comment was poor The single irreversible step. Everything before this is reversible; this is not.

## Pre-flight checklist — all of it, before flipping

- [ ] `paigasus-kernel`, `paigasus-proto`, `paigasus-proto-derive` free on [crates.io](<http://crates.io>)
- [ ] `paigasus-kernel`, `paigasus-proto`, `paigasus-py-bindings` free on PyPI
- [ ] the `@paigasus` npm scope owned by this project
- [ ] **no workspace member name squatted on [crates.io](<http://crates.io>)** — with `git_only` unset, release-plz performs a registry lookup for *every* member name (`paigasus-logging`, `paigasus-observability`, …), so a squatted name would silently become the version-comparison baseline
- [ ] the repository is **public** — `docs/ops/RUNBOOK-go-public.md` documents a flip not yet executed, so every published `repository` / `homepage` URL currently 404s
- [ ] `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` **repository secret exists**, issued from the **existing Paigasus bot GitHub App** (reuse it — do not create a second App). It needs `contents: write` + `pull-requests: write` on this repo.

That is deliberate (an unguarded job would have reddened `main` on every push), but it means the release path is silently inert until this is done, with nothing in CI to say so. Create it as soon as <issue id="58a95803-beac-456d-90da-1b13eec12279" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-576/release-activation-a-kernel-family-010-floor-repoversion-lockstep-gate">SMA-576</issue> merges if you want to observe the job at all — the item below depends on it.

## Expected first-release behaviour

release-plz's baseline is the [**crates.io**](<http://crates.io>) **registry**, not git tags — `ci/release-parity/ecosystems/release-plz.sh:43` sets `git_only = true` precisely to *avoid* the registry lookup for fixture crates, and `rs/release-plz.toml` sets no `git_only`. For a package absent from the registry, the expected behaviour is to treat it as new and propose the **manifest version** — `0.1.0`, no bump.

Do not hand-place a `*-vX.Y.Z` tag to seed release-plz's tracking. [crates.io](<http://crates.io>) supports only `cargo yank` (never delete, never reuse); PyPI supports delete-but-never-reuse; npm supports unpublish within 72 hours only. A wrong publish is a permanent version burn in two of three registries.

{"id":"SMA-596","title":"ci: proto's agent-mode NDJSON breaks $(proto bin ...), so the three release-parity gates abort inconclusive locally","description":"Found while measuring the moon 2.5.3 bump (<issue id="7d449baa-0224-4744-8897-6956abdfb5e7" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-595/upgrade-moon-232-253-and-re-measure-the-affected-graph-claims-it">SMA-595</issue>). **Not caused by that bump** — measured identical on proto 0.58.1 and 0.61.1.

## The hole

`proto` prints **NDJSON on stdout** when it detects an agent environment, starting with a preamble line:

```
{"type":"message","message":"Detected an AI agent environment, printing as NDJSON. Trace logs are written to stderr, while user-facing logs are written to stdout."}
{"type":"message","message":"/Users/…/.proto/tools/release-plz/0.3.158/release-plz"}
```

`ci/release-parity/ecosystems/release-plz.sh:16` captures that:

```bash
RELEASE_PLZ_BIN="$( (cd "$_RP_REPO_ROOT" && proto bin release-plz) 2>/dev/null || command -v release-plz || echo release-plz )"
```

`RELEASE_PLZ_BIN` becomes a JSON blob instead of a path. The `2>/dev/null` does not help — the NDJSON goes to **stdout**, not stderr. The `||` fallbacks never fire either, because `proto bin` **exits 0**; it succeeded, it just spoke a different language.

## Why it matters

All three `repo:release-parity*` gates then abort:

```
line 103: {"type":"message",...}: No such file or directory
FATAL [neg-fix-bang]: run_update failed
negative-control INCONCLUSIVE: infrastructure error (rc=2)
```

That is **rc=2 (harness broke), not rc=1 (gate reported red)** — the distinction <issue id="0ef07e2a-4b63-45ab-892c-d3187bc4ad3d" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-530/ci-run-the-negative-control-self-test-of-release-parity-in-ci">SMA-530</issue> built the negative controls around. So the failure mode is the gate saying "I could not run", which is correct behaviour on its part, but it means:

**No agent session can locally verify the three** `release-parity*` **gates.** Every agent-driven `moon run repo:release-parity` in this repo has been inconclusive, silently, for as long as the agent-detection has existed in proto.

CI has no agent detection, so it has never appeared there and CI results are unaffected.

## Measured

| Setup | `proto bin release-plz` |
| -- | -- |
| proto 0.58.1, agent env | NDJSON (2 lines) |
| proto 0.61.1, agent env | NDJSON (2 lines) |
| proto 0.61.1, `AI_AGENT`/`CLAUDECODE`/`CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` unset | bare path |

With those three variables unset, all three gates pass. That is the current workaround, documented in CLAUDE.md by <issue id="7d449baa-0224-4744-8897-6956abdfb5e7" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-595/upgrade-moon-232-253-and-re-measure-the-affected-graph-claims-it">SMA-595</issue>.

## Shape of a fix

Options, roughly in order of preference:

1. **Make the resolution NDJSON-proof.** Parse the last line and unwrap `.message` when the output is JSON, or resolve the binary without `proto bin` at all (the shim on `PATH` already works: `command -v release-plz` is the existing fallback and would have been correct here).
2. **Force plain output.** Check whether proto honours a flag or env var to suppress agent mode; if one exists, set it in the gate scripts rather than relying on callers to unset three variables.
3. **Assert the resolved path is a file. **`[ -x "$RELEASE_PLZ_BIN" ]` immediately after resolution, so a malformed capture fails loudly at the assignment rather than 90 lines later as a confusing `No such file or directory`.

Option 3 is worth doing regardless of 1 or 2 — it converts a silent class of breakage into an immediate, readable error.

## Audit the rest

`grep -rn 'proto bin' ci/` — any other gate that captures `$(proto bin …)` has the same hole. Check whether `CARGO_BIN` (`release-plz.sh:19`, uses `command -v cargo`) and the other ecosystem scripts are affected too.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The three `repo:release-parity*` gates run to a real verdict in an agent session, with no environment variables unset by hand.
2. Proven: run them in an agent session before the fix (inconclusive, rc=2) and after (pass), and record both.
3. A malformed binary resolution fails at the point of resolution with a readable message, not downstream.
4. Every other `$(proto bin …)` capture in `ci/` is audited and either fixed or shown not to be affected.
5. CLAUDE.md's <issue id="7d449baa-0224-4744-8897-6956abdfb5e7" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-595/upgrade-moon-232-253-and-re-measure-the-affected-graph-claims-it">SMA-595</issue> gotcha is updated to point at the fix instead of the unset workaround.

## Context

* <issue id="7d449baa-0224-4744-8897-6956abdfb5e7" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-595/upgrade-moon-232-253-and-re-measure-the-affected-graph-claims-it">SMA-595</issue> (moon 2.5.3 / proto 0.61.1 bump) — where this was found; PR 175.
* <issue id="0ef07e2a-4b63-45ab-892c-d3187bc4ad3d" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-530/ci-run-the-negative-control-self-test-of-release-parity-in-ci">SMA-530</issue> — the negative-control design whose rc=1 vs rc=2 distinction surfaced it.","projectMilestone":{"id":"0bc8770f-896e-40bc-a156-e0f92b23faf1","name":"MVP"},"priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-596/ci-protos-agent-mode-ndjson-breaks-dollarproto-bin-so-the-three","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-596-ci-protos-agent-mode-ndjson-breaks-proto-bin-so-the-three","createdAt":"2026-08-28T19:44:13.645Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-28T20:11:34.630Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:release","area:ci"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"46bb932e-d4b2-4e1a-8a2a-48ca21321735","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-08-28T19:44:13.645Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","assignee":"Sven Maschek","assigneeId":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Polyglot","projectId":"94351cc4-6a23-4c34-a043-2e7f1bfd9ae4","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-539","title":"repo: lint the inline bash in workflows (pinned shellcheck)","description":"## Context

Follow-up to <issue id="4b65db83-2db5-4034-a0b3-749000d8fbb6" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-525/repo-gate-workflow-yaml-with-actionlint-a-malformed-paths-filter-fails">SMA-525</issue> (limitation L3), which added the `repo:actionlint` gate.

actionlint shells out to `shellcheck` for `run:` blocks whenever it finds one on PATH. <issue id="4b65db83-2db5-4034-a0b3-749000d8fbb6" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-525/repo-gate-workflow-yaml-with-actionlint-a-malformed-paths-filter-fails">SMA-525</issue> **disabled that explicitly** (`-shellcheck= -pyflakes=`) because leaving it opportunistic makes the gate's strictness a property of the host: 0.11.0 via homebrew locally, whatever `ubuntu-latest` currently ships in CI, possibly nothing on a fresh box. An issue whose whole purpose was making a silent failure loud should not ship a sub-check that varies by machine.

So `ci.yml` and `prebuild.yml` carry roughly 120 lines of unlinted inline bash — including `sudo rm -rf /usr/local/lib/android /usr/share/dotnet …` in ci.yml's disk-reclaim step.

## Why this is not just "pin shellcheck"

Pinning it via proto was considered and rejected in <issue id="4b65db83-2db5-4034-a0b3-749000d8fbb6" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-525/repo-gate-workflow-yaml-with-actionlint-a-malformed-paths-filter-fails">SMA-525</issue>'s D2 for a concrete reason: as of 2026-08-16 the `v0.11.0` release publishes **13 archives and no checksums asset**. A `.proto/plugins/shellcheck.toml` would therefore be the first vendored tool in this repo downloaded without integrity verification — a posture regression in a repo that pins action SHAs, runs osv-scanner, and enforces cargo-deny.

That trade deserves its own decision rather than riding along on an unrelated issue.

## Options to weigh

* Pin via proto anyway, accepting an unchecksummed download (and say so explicitly in the plugin header).
* Pin a checksum by hand in the vendored plugin, if proto's TOML schema allows a literal digest.
* Install shellcheck in CI only, from a checksummed source, and keep the local gate shellcheck-free — accepting the local/CI divergence but making it deliberate and documented.
* Leave it disabled and lint the inline bash a different way (extract the long `run:` blocks into `ci/*.sh` files, which the existing tooling already covers).

The last option may be the best of them: `ci/actionlint/run.sh` and `ci/osv/run.sh` already prove that extracted scripts get shellchecked properly.

## Acceptance criteria

* The inline bash in `.github/workflows/**` is linted by something deterministic — same result on a dev box and in CI.
* Whatever is chosen, the integrity story is written down where the next person will find it.
* No new unchecksummed download lands without an explicit, commented justification.","projectMilestone":{"id":"0bc8770f-896e-40bc-a156-e0f92b23faf1","name":"MVP"},"priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-539/repo-lint-the-inline-bash-in-workflows-pinned-shellcheck","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-539-repo-lint-the-inline-bash-in-workflows-pinned-shellcheck","createdAt":"2026-08-16T20:31:00.030Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-23T16:07:08.597Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":[],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"46bb932e-d4b2-4e1a-8a2a-48ca21321735","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-08-16T20:31:00.030Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Polyglot","projectId":"94351cc4-6a23-4c34-a043-2e7f1bfd9ae4","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-554","title":"repo: pin ci.yml's moon ci invocation lines as exact literals instead of pattern-matching them","description":"## Context

Follow-up to <issue id="6a49f7cf-951d-433f-b264-6ab7cb728bea" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-541/repo-assert-every-repo-gate-is-actually-wired-into-ciymls-moon-ci">SMA-541</issue>. Its C5 check asserts that `ci.yml`'s `moon ci` invocations are actually handed the whole `T` array. It does this by **matching the invocation line with a regex**, and that approach was bypassed **four separate times** during <issue id="6a49f7cf-951d-433f-b264-6ab7cb728bea" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-541/repo-assert-every-repo-gate-is-actually-wired-into-ciymls-moon-ci">SMA-541</issue>'s own review — each bypass verified real before it was fixed:

1. `moon ci "${T[@]:0:5}" …` — subsetted array (the original motivation)
2. `moon ci --base origin/main "${T[@]:0:5}" …` — subsetted behind a leading flag; seen by neither C5 nor `assert_include_relations`
3. `echo moon ci "${T[@]}" …` and `moon    ci "${T[@]:0:5}" …` — non-executing, and multi-space
4. `moon ci "${T[@]:0:5}" …  # restore "${T[@]}" later` — the expansion supplied by a trailing comment

All five variants are now red and the fixes are sound. **The pattern is the point of this issue**: textual matching of a shell line has a long tail, and each review round produced another member of it. There is no reason to believe the fifth does not exist.

## The evidence for the fix

<issue id="6a49f7cf-951d-433f-b264-6ab7cb728bea" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-541/repo-assert-every-repo-gate-is-actually-wired-into-ciymls-moon-ci">SMA-541</issue> contains a controlled comparison. Two checks match text:

|  | Approach | Bypasses found |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **C4** (`RUN_SH_CALL_SITES`) | exact literals | **1** — and the fix was to make it *more* literal, adding the `\|\| NEG_RC=1` suffix |
| **C5** (`MOON_CI_LINE_RE`) | pattern matching | **4** |

Every C5 bypass was "the pattern did not describe the thing someone wrote". An exact-literal comparison has no tail to enumerate: there is no clever spelling of a string that is not that string.

## Sketch

In `ci/affected-graph/ci_targets.py`:

1. Replace the `MOON_CI_LINE_RE` + `T_ARRAY_EXPANSION` + `_strip_comment` machinery with an exact expected-literal set for the two invocation lines (including indentation).
2. Keep `EXPECTED_MOON_CI_INVOCATIONS` — the count floor is what catches a line vanishing entirely, which an exact-match set cannot see on its own.
3. Delete the fixtures that only exist to probe the pattern's edges, and keep the ones asserting the count floor and the two-invocation contract.
4. Update the design doc's C5 entry and `ci/affected-graph/README.md`.

## Trade-off, stated

Any legitimate edit to those two lines reds the gate until someone updates the constant. That is intended: an edit to how CI invokes its entire gate graph *should* stop and make a human look. Those two lines have not changed in the repo's history.

## Acceptance criteria

* Each of the four bypasses above still fails the gate, kept as fixtures.
* A legitimate edit to an invocation line fails with a message naming the expected literal and the file to update.
* Deleting one of the two invocations still fails, via the count floor.
* No `repo:*` gate's behaviour changes on an unmutated tree.","projectMilestone":{"id":"0bc8770f-896e-40bc-a156-e0f92b23faf1","name":"MVP"},"priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-554/repo-pin-ciymls-moon-ci-invocation-lines-as-exact-literals-instead-of","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-554-repo-pin-ciymls-moon-ci-invocation-lines-as-exact-literals","createdAt":"2026-08-19T14:51:40.864Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-23T16:07:01.110Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":[],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"46bb932e-d4b2-4e1a-8a2a-48ca21321735","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-08-19T14:51:40.864Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Polyglot","projectId":"94351cc4-6a23-4c34-a043-2e7f1bfd9ae4","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-555","title":"repo: lint ci/**/*.py with ruff — the convention exists but no gate enforces it","description":"## Context

Surfaced during <issue id="6a49f7cf-951d-433f-b264-6ab7cb728bea" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-541/repo-assert-every-repo-gate-is-actually-wired-into-ciymls-moon-ci">SMA-541</issue>. The Python under `ci/` is expected to comply with the repo's Ruff rule set, but **nothing enforces it**: `.moon/tasks/python.yml` runs `uv run ruff check .` scoped to the `py` project, and `ci/affected-graph/*.py` is outside that scope. No other task lints it.

{"id":"SMA-552","title":"rust: --locked is unenforceable across the Moon graph, so a build can silently re-resolve the lockfile","description":"Split out of <issue id="da2c0eef-0d09-4c91-b319-d73df57994c5" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-546/rust-a-dep-bump-still-ships-unlinked-clippy-neither-links-the-cdylibs">SMA-546</issue>, which investigated `--locked` on the three FFI build tasks, measured that it **cannot work at that level**, and deliberately deferred it rather than half-ship it. See the "`--locked` was investigated and deliberately deferred" section of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-17-sma-546-ffi-workspace-inputs-design.md` for the full write-up.

## The claim that does not hold

<issue id="108c3e22-01a6-41be-9939-afe49a0b3035" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-534/rust-a-cargolock-only-change-lints-nothing-so-a-dep-bumps-clippy-break">SMA-534</issue> established the principle: without `--locked`, cargo silently re-resolves and **rewrites** an inconsistent `Cargo.lock`, so a gate no longer proves anything about the resolution the PR actually ships. It made `lint` (`cargo clippy --locked`) enforce that. This repo has already shipped a Dependabot lockfile resolved from 3 of 11 workspace members.

That principle is currently enforced for exactly one compile gate. Everything else in the graph can re-resolve behind it.

## Two independent root causes, both measured

**1. The FFI tools pre-resolve. **`napi build` and `wasm-pack build` each run an **un-flagged** `cargo metadata` before their `cargo build`. That call rewrites a stale lockfile, so the subsequent `cargo build --locked` always finds it fresh and can never fail.

Measured on a worktree with the lock made genuinely stale (a dependency added to `rs/crates/bindings/paigasus-wasm/Cargo.toml`):

| invocation | exit | `rs/Cargo.lock` after |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `cargo build --locked` (control) | 101 — *"cannot update the lock file … because* `--locked` *was passed"* | clean |
| `wasm-pack build … -- --locked` | **0** | **REWRITTEN** |
| `napi build … -- --locked` | **0** | **REWRITTEN** |
| `MATURIN_PEP517_ARGS=--locked uv sync --reinstall-package …` | 101 | clean |

Note the py/maturin path is **already correct** — maturin forwards its cargo options to `cargo metadata` too. Only the two ts tools are affected.

**2. The graph pre-resolves.** Even with a task-local `cargo metadata --locked` fail-fast guard (which does work in isolation — verified in both directions), the shared `build` task in `.moon/tasks/rust.yml` is a plain unflagged `cargo build`, inherited by all thirteen crates and scheduled **ahead** of dependents by `deps: ['^:build']`. It rewrites a stale lock itself, so whether any task-local guard fires is **order-dependent**.

## Why it matters now

`rs/Cargo.lock` became a declared **input** of `paigasus-kernel-ts:{build,test}` and `paigasus-kernel-py:test` in <issue id="da2c0eef-0d09-4c91-b319-d73df57994c5" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-546/rust-a-dep-bump-still-ships-unlinked-clippy-neither-links-the-cdylibs">SMA-546</issue> (and of all thirteen `lint` tasks in <issue id="108c3e22-01a6-41be-9939-afe49a0b3035" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-534/rust-a-cargolock-only-change-lints-nothing-so-a-dep-bumps-clippy-break">SMA-534</issue>). A task that rewrites a file it declares as an input:

* invalidates the hash Moon recorded **before** execution, so the cache key describes a tree that no longer exists; and
* races `repo:deny` (`moon.yml:23`), `repo:wasm-getrandom-free` (`moon.yml:250`) and `repo:nats-permissions` (`moon.yml:229`), which read `rs/Cargo.lock` concurrently in the same `moon ci` graph.

Worst case today is a spurious cache miss rather than a wrong result, which is why this is Medium and not Urgent — but the guarantee <issue id="108c3e22-01a6-41be-9939-afe49a0b3035" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-534/rust-a-cargolock-only-change-lints-nothing-so-a-dep-bumps-clippy-break">SMA-534</issue> set out to establish is currently only partial.

## Options to weigh

1. `--locked` **on the shared Rust** `build` **task** in `.moon/tasks/rust.yml` — closes root cause 2 for all thirteen crates in one line. Consider `test` (`cargo nextest run`) too. Costs: reds any PR whose manifest and lock are out of sync (arguably correct, and matches `lint`), changes local dev ergonomics repo-wide, and re-keys every Rust task.
2. **A repo-scoped** `cargo metadata --locked` **preflight gate** — one cheap check that the lock is consistent, independent of which tasks run. Does not stop a rewrite, only detects the inconsistency.
3. **Accept and document** — record the divergence explicitly so nobody re-derives it. This is the current state, via the <issue id="da2c0eef-0d09-4c91-b319-d73df57994c5" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-546/rust-a-dep-bump-still-ships-unlinked-clippy-neither-links-the-cdylibs">SMA-546</issue> spec.

## Verification notes for whoever picks this up

* To make the lock genuinely stale, add a dependency to a member manifest. `git status --short rs/Cargo.lock` **is the only authoritative check for a rewrite** — do *not* grep the lockfile for the package name, because common crates (`itoa`, etc.) are already present as transitive deps and the grep will mislead you.
* Sending a bogus flag through a tool proves the argument **reaches** cargo; it does **not** prove `--locked` bites. Only the staleness experiment distinguishes them. That mistake is what put a false claim into the <issue id="da2c0eef-0d09-4c91-b319-d73df57994c5" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-546/rust-a-dep-bump-still-ships-unlinked-clippy-neither-links-the-cdylibs">SMA-546</issue> spec in the first place.
* Current `--locked` users, for reference: `lint` (`cargo clippy --locked`) is the only compile gate; `repo:publish-metadata` uses it for `cargo package --list` / `cargo publish --dry-run`; `.github/workflows/prebuild.yml` uses `cargo install --locked` for cargo-zigbuild, which is a tool install rather than a workspace build.","projectMilestone":{"id":"0bc8770f-896e-40bc-a156-e0f92b23faf1","name":"MVP"},"priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-552/rust-locked-is-unenforceable-across-the-moon-graph-so-a-build-can","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-552-rust-locked-is-unenforceable-across-the-moon-graph-so-a","createdAt":"2026-08-19T07:38:09.122Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-23T16:05:19.182Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:deps","area:ci","Bug"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"46bb932e-d4b2-4e1a-8a2a-48ca21321735","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-08-19T07:38:09.122Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Polyglot","projectId":"94351cc4-6a23-4c34-a043-2e7f1bfd9ae4","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-599","title":"repo: nothing enforces that every cargo-from-rs task keys on rs/.cargo/config.toml","description":"Follow-up to <issue id="ce12a763-8515-4658-9114-c9760bf90576" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-594/rust-rscargoconfigtoml-is-read-by-the-ffi-builds-and-keyed-on-by">SMA-594</issue> (merged as PR 176, `d3dd101`). That issue established a rule and fixed every instance of it. **Nothing enforces the rule**, and the failure mode is already demonstrated.

## The rule <issue id="ce12a763-8515-4658-9114-c9760bf90576" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-594/rust-rscargoconfigtoml-is-read-by-the-ffi-builds-and-keyed-on-by">SMA-594</issue> established

> A task that runs cargo with cwd inside `rs/` keys on `rs/.cargo/config.toml`.

The file sets `rustflags` for the two `*-apple-darwin` targets, and cargo discovers it by walking up from the working directory — so every such task reads it.

## Why the rule is currently a convention, not an invariant

Measured on the merged branch: editing that file selects **61** tasks. Only **16** of those declarations are asserted by anything.

| Assertion | What it covers |
| -- | -- |
| A4 (`check_task_inputs(..., "lint", WORKSPACE_LINT_INPUTS)`) | 13 crates' `lint` |
| A5 (`check_ffi_inputs`) | the 3 derived FFI tasks |
| — | the 39 `build` / `build-release` / `test` declarations |
| — | the 3 `repo:*` gates |

`check_task_inputs` is called only for `lint` and `fmt`. `repo:input-liveness` proves that **declared** inputs are live; it never proves that **needed** ones are declared.

## The failure mode is not hypothetical

<issue id="ce12a763-8515-4658-9114-c9760bf90576" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-594/rust-rscargoconfigtoml-is-read-by-the-ffi-builds-and-keyed-on-by">SMA-594</issue>'s own implementation missed three `repo:*` tasks that compile Rust from inside `rs/` — `repo:parity-corpus-drift` (`moon.yml:209`), `repo:observability-drift` (`:228`) and `repo:nats-permissions` (`:253`). They were found by an adversarial review, not by any gate. `parity-corpus-drift`'s own comment says *"Run the generator crate-scoped from rs/ so rs/.cargo/config.toml is in scope"* — the file was documented as influencing the task and was still not one of its inputs.

A future `repo:*` task that runs cargo from `rs/` can omit the input today and nothing reds. This is the same shape as <issue id="914a9b1a-1be1-4212-9b43-cbb488a8f219" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-528/ci-moon-ci-include-relations-does-not-cascade-tasks-so-no-kernel">SMA-528</issue> and <issue id="9f3d9c67-105f-43e3-9057-78b8726c2e39" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-560/repo-the-pyts-wrappers-rust-source-inputs-are-the-adr-0005-guarantee">SMA-560</issue>: a real invariant living only in prose.

## Shape of a fix

A5's `derive_ffi_tasks` is the pattern to copy, and its anti-vacuity design is the part that matters:

1. **Derive** the task set — scan every task's resolved `command` + `args` + `script` for a cargo invocation whose cwd resolves inside `rs/`. A derived set covers a new task on day one; a hand-written list is exactly what missed the three gates above.
2. **Floor it.** A5 pairs its derivation with `REQUIRED_FFI_TASKS` precisely because a derived set that shrinks to empty prints PASS while asserting nothing. This check needs the same: name a handful of tasks that MUST appear in the derived set.
3. Decide what to do about `cargo tree` — `repo:wasm-getrandom-free` runs it from `rs/` and is deliberately excluded, because it resolves dependencies and never applies rustflags. That exclusion currently rests on the file's *current content*: a future `[source]` replacement or `[build]` key would change `cargo tree`'s output. Either encode the exclusion with a reason, or widen the rule and accept the over-trigger.
4. `repo:deny` and `repo:machete` run cargo from the repo **root**, so the file is not on cargo's upward walk. They are correctly out of scope.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Adding a task that runs cargo from `rs/` without declaring the input fails the gate.
2. The gate is proven to red by a mutation, not merely observed to pass: remove the input from one of the three `repo:*` gates and confirm the named failure, then restore.
3. The derived set has an anti-vacuity floor, and emptying the derivation is proven to fail.
4. The `cargo tree` exclusion is either encoded with a stated reason or removed, and the choice is recorded.
5. `ci/affected-graph/run.sh` reports no expected-set movement, or the movement is explained.

## Context

`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-sma-592-codegen-and-input-affectedness-residue-design.md` §3 and §8 carry the design and the recorded limitation. {"id":"SMA-600","title":"py: a PyO3 stub-drift gate — the hand-written .pyi can disagree with the Rust and nothing fails","description":"Owns the real fix for <issue id="46186b0d-8584-4bad-a3aa-2fe8adb80d71" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-535/py-pytypecheck-does-not-propagate-from-rust-so-a-pyo3-signature-change">SMA-535</issue>. Filed separately because <issue id="46186b0d-8584-4bad-a3aa-2fe8adb80d71" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-535/py-pytypecheck-does-not-propagate-from-rust-so-a-pyo3-signature-change">SMA-535</issue>'s title and body describe a fix that **cannot work**, and re-scoping it in place would lose the record of why.

## The gap

`rs/crates/bindings/paigasus-py-bindings/paigasus_py_bindings.pyi` is **hand-written** — a tracked source file with an SPDX header and no codegen banner, listed in the crate's Cargo `include` (`Cargo.toml:20`) so it ships in the wheel and the sdist.

It is basedpyright's **entire** view of the PyO3 surface. A `#[pyfunction]` signature change with no stub update therefore leaves the stub self-consistent, and the type checker passes. Nothing else compares the two.

## Why <issue id="46186b0d-8584-4bad-a3aa-2fe8adb80d71" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-535/py-pytypecheck-does-not-propagate-from-rust-so-a-pyo3-signature-change">SMA-535</issue>'s filed fix cannot close this

Adding `/rs/...` inputs to `py:typecheck` buys **scheduling with no coverage**. Two independent reasons, either sufficient:

1. basedpyright reads the stub, never the Rust. No input list changes what it reads.
2. `.moon/tasks/python.yml` runs plain `uv run basedpyright` with no `--reinstall-package`, and `uv run` is measured in-repo to serve a **cached wheel** — so even the stub it reads is the installed copy, not the working tree's.

This was scoped into the <issue id="1e1cb2c8-fbb9-4f23-9bdc-00bc5b91030a" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-592/repo-a-bufgenyaml-or-codegen-plugin-bump-regenerates-output-but">SMA-592</issue>/<issue id="ce12a763-8515-4658-9114-c9760bf90576" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-594/rust-rscargoconfigtoml-is-read-by-the-ffi-builds-and-keyed-on-by">SMA-594</issue> branch, then removed during design. Reasoning is recorded as a comment on <issue id="46186b0d-8584-4bad-a3aa-2fe8adb80d71" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-535/py-pytypecheck-does-not-propagate-from-rust-so-a-pyo3-signature-change">SMA-535</issue>.

## What <issue id="ce12a763-8515-4658-9114-c9760bf90576" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-594/rust-rscargoconfigtoml-is-read-by-the-ffi-builds-and-keyed-on-by">SMA-594</issue> already did, and why it is not this

PR 176 (`d3dd101`) closed a *neighbouring* gap: the `.pyi` was in no task's inputs at all, so editing the interface contract did not re-run `paigasus-kernel-py:test`. It now does, and assertion A7 demands every `{upstream}/*.pyi` found on disk.

**That makes a stub edit re-run the smoke test. It does not make a stub that disagrees with the Rust fail.** Do not read A7's clause as partial coverage here.

## Shape of a fix — compare three sets

Measured on `main` today, all three agree at 12, so the gate lands green on an unmutated tree:

| Set | Source | Count |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `#[pyfunction]` idents | `paigasus-py-bindings/src/lib.rs` | 12 |
| `wrap_pyfunction!` registrations | the module init in the same file | 12 |
| `def` names | `paigasus_py_bindings.pyi` | 12 |

All three must match. Two of the three is not enough: a function that is declared and registered but missing from the stub is invisible to Python consumers' type checking, while one declared and stubbed but never registered is an `AttributeError` at import.

Whether to compare **signatures** as well as names is the open design question. Names catch the common drift (add a function, forget the stub); parameter types and arity would catch more but need a real parser rather than a regex, and the stub uses Python types where the Rust uses `f64`/`String`.

## The ts side is a different problem — do not merge them

`rs/crates/bindings/paigasus-node-bindings/index.d.ts` opens with `/* auto-generated by NAPI-RS */`. Because it is **generated**, its drift is caught by regenerating and diffing, not by comparing sets — which is <issue id="1f3421f7-12a7-4adc-9de7-d8093041340e" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-434/add-a-ci-drift-check-for-committed-ffi-binding-glue-napi-wasm">SMA-434</issue>'s shape, not this one.

<issue id="db68b2ed-ddd4-47d0-8da2-aac3b4449df8" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-536/ts-typecheck-carries-no-deps-and-cannot-propagate-only-a-build">SMA-536</issue> (`ts:typecheck` carries no deps and cannot propagate) is the *scheduling* half on that side and is related but distinct. Three issues, three shapes:

* **this issue** — hand-written stub vs Rust: compare three sets
* <issue id="1f3421f7-12a7-4adc-9de7-d8093041340e" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-434/add-a-ci-drift-check-for-committed-ffi-binding-glue-napi-wasm">SMA-434</issue> — generated napi/wasm glue: regenerate and diff
* <issue id="db68b2ed-ddd4-47d0-8da2-aac3b4449df8" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-536/ts-typecheck-carries-no-deps-and-cannot-propagate-only-a-build">SMA-536</issue> — ts:typecheck scheduling

## Acceptance criteria

1. Adding a `#[pyfunction]` without stubbing it fails the gate.
2. Removing a `wrap_pyfunction!` registration while keeping the declaration and the stub fails the gate.
3. Deleting a `def` from the stub while the Rust keeps the function fails the gate.
4. Each of those three is proven to red by mutation on a scratch copy, then restored — a gate that cannot fail is worse than no gate.
5. The gate is selected by a change to either the Rust or the stub. Note `repo:input-liveness` and the reachability rule: whatever pins it must list the paths it reads among its own inputs.
6. Whether signatures are compared as well as names is decided explicitly and recorded, not left ambiguous.
7. If it lands as a new `repo:*` task, it joins `ci.yml`'s `T=(…)` array **and** CLAUDE.md's marker-delimited command, or `repo:affected-smoke` reds.

## Context

{"id":"SMA-600","title":"py: a PyO3 stub-drift gate — the hand-written .pyi can disagree with the Rust and nothing fails","description":"Owns the real fix for <issue id="46186b0d-8584-4bad-a3aa-2fe8adb80d71" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-535/py-pytypecheck-does-not-propagate-from-rust-so-a-pyo3-signature-change">SMA-535</issue>. Filed separately because <issue id="46186b0d-8584-4bad-a3aa-2fe8adb80d71" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-535/py-pytypecheck-does-not-propagate-from-rust-so-a-pyo3-signature-change">SMA-535</issue>'s title and body describe a fix that **cannot work**, and re-scoping it in place would lose the record of why.

## The gap

`rs/crates/bindings/paigasus-py-bindings/paigasus_py_bindings.pyi` is **hand-written** — a tracked source file with an SPDX header and no codegen banner, listed in the crate's Cargo `include` (`Cargo.toml:20`) so it ships in the wheel and the sdist.

It is basedpyright's **entire** view of the PyO3 surface. A `#[pyfunction]` signature change with no stub update therefore leaves the stub self-consistent, and the type checker passes. Nothing else compares the two.

## Why <issue id="46186b0d-8584-4bad-a3aa-2fe8adb80d71" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-535/py-pytypecheck-does-not-propagate-from-rust-so-a-pyo3-signature-change">SMA-535</issue>'s filed fix cannot close this

Adding `/rs/...` inputs to `py:typecheck` buys **scheduling with no coverage**. Two independent reasons, either sufficient:

1. basedpyright reads the stub, never the Rust. No input list changes what it reads.
2. `.moon/tasks/python.yml` runs plain `uv run basedpyright` with no `--reinstall-package`, and `uv run` is measured in-repo to serve a **cached wheel** — so even the stub it reads is the installed copy, not the working tree's.

This was scoped into the <issue id="1e1cb2c8-fbb9-4f23-9bdc-00bc5b91030a" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-592/repo-a-bufgenyaml-or-codegen-plugin-bump-regenerates-output-but">SMA-592</issue>/<issue id="ce12a763-8515-4658-9114-c9760bf90576" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-594/rust-rscargoconfigtoml-is-read-by-the-ffi-builds-and-keyed-on-by">SMA-594</issue> branch, then removed during design. Reasoning is recorded as a comment on <issue id="46186b0d-8584-4bad-a3aa-2fe8adb80d71" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-535/py-pytypecheck-does-not-propagate-from-rust-so-a-pyo3-signature-change">SMA-535</issue>.

## What <issue id="ce12a763-8515-4658-9114-c9760bf90576" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-594/rust-rscargoconfigtoml-is-read-by-the-ffi-builds-and-keyed-on-by">SMA-594</issue> already did, and why it is not this

PR 176 (`d3dd101`) closed a *neighbouring* gap: the `.pyi` was in no task's inputs at all, so editing the interface contract did not re-run `paigasus-kernel-py:test`. It now does, and assertion A7 demands every `{upstream}/*.pyi` found on disk.

**That makes a stub edit re-run the smoke test. It does not make a stub that disagrees with the Rust fail.** Do not read A7's clause as partial coverage here.

## Shape of a fix — compare three sets

Measured on `main` today, all three agree at 12, so the gate lands green on an unmutated tree:

| Set | Source | Count |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `#[pyfunction]` idents | `paigasus-py-bindings/src/lib.rs` | 12 |
| `wrap_pyfunction!` registrations | the module init in the same file | 12 |
| `def` names | `paigasus_py_bindings.pyi` | 12 |

All three must match. Two of the three is not enough: a function that is declared and registered but missing from the stub is invisible to Python consumers' type checking, while one declared and stubbed but never registered is an `AttributeError` at import.

Whether to compare **signatures** as well as names is the open design question. Names catch the common drift (add a function, forget the stub); parameter types and arity would catch more but need a real parser rather than a regex, and the stub uses Python types where the Rust uses `f64`/`String`.

## The ts side is a different problem — do not merge them

`rs/crates/bindings/paigasus-node-bindings/index.d.ts` opens with `/* auto-generated by NAPI-RS */`. Because it is **generated**, its drift is caught by regenerating and diffing, not by comparing sets — which is <issue id="1f3421f7-12a7-4adc-9de7-d8093041340e" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-434/add-a-ci-drift-check-for-committed-ffi-binding-glue-napi-wasm">SMA-434</issue>'s shape, not this one.

<issue id="db68b2ed-ddd4-47d0-8da2-aac3b4449df8" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-536/ts-typecheck-carries-no-deps-and-cannot-propagate-only-a-build">SMA-536</issue> (`ts:typecheck` carries no deps and cannot propagate) is the *scheduling* half on that side and is related but distinct. Three issues, three shapes:

* **this issue** — hand-written stub vs Rust: compare three sets
* <issue id="1f3421f7-12a7-4adc-9de7-d8093041340e" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-434/add-a-ci-drift-check-for-committed-ffi-binding-glue-napi-wasm">SMA-434</issue> — generated napi/wasm glue: regenerate and diff
* <issue id="db68b2ed-ddd4-47d0-8da2-aac3b4449df8" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-536/ts-typecheck-carries-no-deps-and-cannot-propagate-only-a-build">SMA-536</issue> — ts:typecheck scheduling

## Acceptance criteria

1. Adding a `#[pyfunction]` without stubbing it fails the gate.
2. Removing a `wrap_pyfunction!` registration while keeping the declaration and the stub fails the gate.
3. Deleting a `def` from the stub while the Rust keeps the function fails the gate.
4. Each of those three is proven to red by mutation on a scratch copy, then restored — a gate that cannot fail is worse than no gate.
5. The gate is selected by a change to either the Rust or the stub. Note `repo:input-liveness` and the reachability rule: whatever pins it must list the paths it reads among its own inputs.
6. Whether signatures are compared as well as names is decided explicitly and recorded, not left ambiguous.
7. If it lands as a new `repo:*` task, it joins `ci.yml`'s `T=(…)` array **and** CLAUDE.md's marker-delimited command, or `repo:affected-smoke` reds.

## Context

`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-sma-592-codegen-and-input-affectedness-residue-design.md` §5 records why <issue id="46186b0d-8584-4bad-a3aa-2fe8adb80d71" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-535/py-pytypecheck-does-not-propagate-from-rust-so-a-pyo3-signature-change">SMA-535</issue> left that branch. <issue id="9f3d9c67-105f-43e3-9057-78b8726c2e39" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-560/repo-the-pyts-wrappers-rust-source-inputs-are-the-adr-0005-guarantee">SMA-560</issue>'s spec §2.1 has the earlier analysis, including the `uv run` cached-wheel measurement.","projectMilestone":{"id":"0bc8770f-896e-40bc-a156-e0f92b23faf1","name":"MVP"},"priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-600/py-a-pyo3-stub-drift-gate-the-hand-written-pyi-can-disagree-with-the","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-600-py-a-pyo3-stub-drift-gate-the-hand-written-pyi-can-disagree","createdAt":"2026-08-28T22:07:58.566Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-28T22:09:03.199Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:ffi","area:ci"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"46bb932e-d4b2-4e1a-8a2a-48ca21321735","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-08-28T22:07:58.566Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Polyglot","projectId":"94351cc4-6a23-4c34-a043-2e7f1bfd9ae4","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-588","title":"iam: twelve Query/Path request extractors answer outside the error envelope","description":"Deferred from <issue id="9a1957cc-7e9d-4298-b1a2-3fd5a78f1df9" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-587/iam-fourteen-http-routes-answer-a-malformed-json-body-outside-the">SMA-587</issue> (see its spec's *Out of scope*). Same class of hole as <issue id="4aee6543-a7cc-481e-8653-5733789b8182" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-586/iam-invalid-prn-is-a-catch-all-sentinel-for-four-unrelated-validation">SMA-586</issue>'s `Path<Uuid>` and <issue id="9a1957cc-7e9d-4298-b1a2-3fd5a78f1df9" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-587/iam-fourteen-http-routes-answer-a-malformed-json-body-outside-the">SMA-587</issue>'s `Json<T>`, third instance.

## The problem

<issue id="9a1957cc-7e9d-4298-b1a2-3fd5a78f1df9" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-587/iam-fourteen-http-routes-answer-a-malformed-json-body-outside-the">SMA-587</issue> made every **body** extractor in `paigasus-iam`'s HTTP adapter answer inside the stable `{"error":{code,message}}` envelope, and added `repo:http-extractor-envelope` to keep it that way. Twelve **non-body** request extractors still escape it:

**Ten** `Query<…>` **bindings** — `?limit=abc` yields axum's plain-text `FailedToDeserializeQueryString` 400 today, with no `error.code`:

| File | Handler |
| -- | -- |
| `api_keys.rs` | list |
| `audit.rs` | list |
| `authz.rs` | list policies |
| `authz.rs` | list role grants |
| `dead_letters.rs` | list |
| `memberships.rs` | list |
| `organizations.rs` | list orgs |
| `organizations.rs` | list teams |
| `service_accounts.rs` | list |
| `teams.rs` | list projects |

**Two** `Path<String>` — not covered by <issue id="4aee6543-a7cc-481e-8653-5733789b8182" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-586/iam-invalid-prn-is-a-catch-all-sentinel-for-four-unrelated-validation">SMA-586</issue>'s `UuidPath` because the segment is not a uuid:

| File | Handler |
| -- | -- |
| `authz.rs` | delete policy (`{id}`) |
| `system_retirement.rs:96` | retire (`{id}`) |

## Why it matters

{"id":"SMA-597","title":"ci: ciReport.json carries no stdout/stderr and a null exitCode, so the documented way to diagnose an unattributed moon failure cannot work","description":"Found while closing out <issue id="7d449baa-0224-4744-8897-6956abdfb5e7" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-595/upgrade-moon-232-253-and-re-measure-the-affected-graph-claims-it">SMA-595</issue> (the moon 2.5.3 bump). Evidence contributed by a second session's run; corroborated against merged source. Not caused by that bump.

## The documented advice

A recurring line in the plan template under `docs/superpowers/plans/` — it appears in **53 of the 104 plan documents on **`main`, just over half the corpus, including <issue id="6a49f7cf-951d-433f-b264-6ab7cb728bea" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-541/repo-assert-every-repo-gate-is-actually-wired-into-ciymls-moon-ci">SMA-541</issue>, <issue id="4b65db83-2db5-4034-a0b3-749000d8fbb6" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-525/repo-gate-workflow-yaml-with-actionlint-a-malformed-paths-filter-fails">SMA-525</issue>, <issue id="0ef6ae1f-52d0-43f4-a004-1d58dde354b6" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-553/repo-assert-every-repo-tasks-inputs-still-match-a-file-a-gate-can-be">SMA-553</issue>, <issue id="9a1957cc-7e9d-4298-b1a2-3fd5a78f1df9" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-587/iam-fourteen-http-routes-answer-a-malformed-json-body-outside-the">SMA-587</issue>, <issue id="864ac3e9-d82f-4f9b-9428-20d04ca2e355" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-521/repo-paigasus-iam-rstest-has-no-retries-and-is-flaky-under-docker">SMA-521</issue> and <issue id="e936f632-4501-4796-9630-ec62f5138b41" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-376/publish-paigasus-kernel-flip-publishtrue-and-set-first-real-version">SMA-376</issue> — says:

> If Moon reports an unattributed "N failed", read `.moon/cache/ciReport.json` and filter with `jq '.actions[] | select(.status == "failed")'`.

**Note this is NOT in CLAUDE.md.** Verified independently by two sessions:

```
$ grep -c ciReport CLAUDE.md CONTRIBUTING.md
CLAUDE.md:0
CONTRIBUTING.md:0
$ grep -rl ciReport docs/superpowers/plans/ | wc -l
53          # on main; a worktree whose branch adds one more plan reports 54
```

It lives in the dated plan documents and in agent session memory. That is why nothing has ever gated it, and it decides where the fix goes: **53 dated historical records are not a corpus anyone should be editing.** Fix the template that keeps emitting the line, and put a corrected procedure somewhere gated.

This issue was first drafted claiming CLAUDE.md carried the advice. It does not. That claim was asserted from recollection, passed between two sessions, and reached a third reader before anyone ran a grep — in a repo whose gates exist precisely to stop assertions that pass for the wrong reason. The correction cost one command. Worth remembering when reading any "X is documented in Y" claim here, this issue's own included.

## Why it cannot work

Measured on a real unattributed failure: the `ciReport.json` entry for the failing task carries no stdout, no stderr, and a null `exitCode`. The report tells you *which* action failed — the part `moon` already prints — and nothing about *why*. The information the advice exists to retrieve is not in the file.

The evidence only exists in the **task log**.

## The measured case

`repo:affected-smoke` aborted at 2.3s (against its usual 6–8s) during a full 27-target `moon ci`. `ciReport.json` yielded nothing usable. The task log carried the whole answer:

```
Error: proto-shim: Failed to execute proto for the shimmed command:
       Permission denied (os error 13)
Please refer to the documentation or ask for support on Discord.
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
    import sys,json; print("\n".join(sorted(p["id"] for p in json.load(sys.stdin)["projects"] …
json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
FATAL [contracts->proto]: moon query failed
== affected-graph guard ABORTED: infrastructure error (rc=2) ==
```

This is exactly the failure <issue id="7d449baa-0224-4744-8897-6956abdfb5e7" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-595/upgrade-moon-232-253-and-re-measure-the-affected-graph-claims-it">SMA-595</issue> recorded as unexplained. <issue id="7d449baa-0224-4744-8897-6956abdfb5e7" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-595/upgrade-moon-232-253-and-re-measure-the-affected-graph-claims-it">SMA-595</issue> consulted the report, found nothing, and shipped the gotcha saying the cause was unknown — a concrete instance of the documented path failing at the moment it was needed.

**Corroboration:** both failure strings match `ci/affected-graph/run.sh` as merged — `FATAL [$label]: moon query failed` in the nested-query error path, and `== affected-graph guard ABORTED: infrastructure error (rc=$ec) ==` in `run_case`'s rc-2 branch. So the log is consistent with the code, not only with the narrative built from it.

Attribution: the failing run and this log excerpt come from the `paigasus-core-3c` session's <issue id="1e1cb2c8-fbb9-4f23-9bdc-00bc5b91030a" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-592/repo-a-bufgenyaml-or-codegen-plugin-bump-regenerates-output-but">SMA-592</issue> acceptance run. The source-string corroboration and the second independent symptom observation come from <issue id="7d449baa-0224-4744-8897-6956abdfb5e7" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-595/upgrade-moon-232-253-and-re-measure-the-affected-graph-claims-it">SMA-595</issue>.

## Why it matters

The advice is not merely useless, it is actively misleading. An agent or a human follows it, gets a `status: "failed"` row with a null `exitCode`, and concludes there is nothing more to find — when the full diagnosis is sitting in the task log. That is how <issue id="7d449baa-0224-4744-8897-6956abdfb5e7" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-595/upgrade-moon-232-253-and-re-measure-the-affected-graph-claims-it">SMA-595</issue> shipped "cause unknown". The failure mode is a confident dead end, not an obvious error.

It also compounds with the `buffer-only-failure` output style: a *passing* task's output is discarded by design, so when a flaky failure does not reproduce, the one run that carried the evidence is gone. Re-running destroys it.

## Shape of a fix

Separable, and the first is worth doing alone:

1. **Correct the guidance.** Establish the actual diagnosis path — the task log, and `moon run <target>` with output streamed — and put it somewhere gated. CLAUDE.md is the candidate; the plan template is where the wrong version keeps getting copied from. Leave the existing dated plans alone: they record what was believed when written.
2. **Check whether the report can carry more.** Confirm against moon 2.5.3 whether `--summary detailed`, a different report field, or the daemon's own logs expose stdout/stderr and a real `exitCode`. If a working invocation exists, document that instead of abandoning the file. If none does, say so explicitly, with the measurement.
3. **Say where task logs live** and how to read one for a specific target, since that is the path that actually works.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The repo carries a diagnosis procedure for an unattributed moon failure that is **demonstrated** to surface the cause — proven against a deliberately failing task, with the output recorded.
2. Whether `ciReport.json` can be made to carry stdout/stderr/`exitCode` on moon 2.5.3 is measured and written down, either way.
3. New plans stop reproducing the broken advice; the plan template is the place to fix that.
4. The interaction with `buffer-only-failure` — that a non-reproducing failure's evidence is lost on re-run — is stated wherever the procedure lands.

* <issue id="26276b8e-6079-4fad-b22f-eab8541c5f17" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-596/ci-protos-agent-mode-ndjson-breaks-dollarproto-bin-so-the-three">SMA-596</issue> — proto's agent-mode NDJSON. **The same tool underlies both**: there, proto's stdout corrupts a caller's parse; here, a proto shim exec failure is the cause the report could not surface. The report tells you *which* action failed — the part `moon` already prints — and nothing about *why*. The information the advice exists to retrieve is not in the file.

The evidence only exists in the **task log**.

## The measured case

`repo:affected-smoke` aborted at 2.3s (against its usual 6–8s) during a full 27-target `moon ci`. `ciReport.json` yielded nothing usable. The task log carried the whole answer:

```
Error: proto-shim: Failed to execute proto for the shimmed command:
       Permission denied (os error 13)
Please refer to the documentation or ask for support on Discord.
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
    import sys,json; print("\n".join(sorted(p["id"] for p in json.load(sys.stdin)["projects"] …
json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
FATAL [contracts->proto]: moon query failed
== affected-graph guard ABORTED: infrastructure error (rc=2) ==
```

This is exactly the failure <issue id="7d449baa-0224-4744-8897-6956abdfb5e7" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-595/upgrade-moon-232-253-and-re-measure-the-affected-graph-claims-it">SMA-595</issue> recorded as unexplained. <issue id="7d449baa-0224-4744-8897-6956abdfb5e7" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-595/upgrade-moon-232-253-and-re-measure-the-affected-graph-claims-it">SMA-595</issue> consulted the report, found nothing, and shipped the gotcha saying the cause was unknown — a concrete instance of the documented path failing at the moment it was needed.

**Corroboration:** both failure strings match `ci/affected-graph/run.sh` as merged — `FATAL [$label]: moon query failed` in the nested-query error path, and `== affected-graph guard ABORTED: infrastructure error (rc=$ec) ==` in `run_case`'s rc-2 branch. So the log is consistent with the code, not only with the narrative built from it.

Attribution: the failing run and this log excerpt come from the `paigasus-core-3c` session's <issue id="1e1cb2c8-fbb9-4f23-9bdc-00bc5b91030a" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-592/repo-a-bufgenyaml-or-codegen-plugin-bump-regenerates-output-but">SMA-592</issue> acceptance run. The source-string corroboration and the second independent symptom observation come from <issue id="7d449baa-0224-4744-8897-6956abdfb5e7" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-595/upgrade-moon-232-253-and-re-measure-the-affected-graph-claims-it">SMA-595</issue>.

## Why it matters

The advice is not merely useless, it is actively misleading. An agent or a human follows it, gets a `status: "failed"` row with a null `exitCode`, and concludes there is nothing more to find — when the full diagnosis is sitting in the task log. That is how <issue id="7d449baa-0224-4744-8897-6956abdfb5e7" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-595/upgrade-moon-232-253-and-re-measure-the-affected-graph-claims-it">SMA-595</issue> shipped "cause unknown". The failure mode is a confident dead end, not an obvious error.

It also compounds with the `buffer-only-failure` output style: a *passing* task's output is discarded by design, so when a flaky failure does not reproduce, the one run that carried the evidence is gone. Re-running destroys it.

## Shape of a fix

Separable, and the first is worth doing alone:

1. **Correct the guidance.** Establish the actual diagnosis path — the task log, and `moon run <target>` with output streamed — and put it somewhere gated. CLAUDE.md is the candidate; the plan template is where the wrong version keeps getting copied from. Leave the existing dated plans alone: they record what was believed when written.
2. **Check whether the report can carry more.** Confirm against moon 2.5.3 whether `--summary detailed`, a different report field, or the daemon's own logs expose stdout/stderr and a real `exitCode`. If a working invocation exists, document that instead of abandoning the file. If none does, say so explicitly, with the measurement.
3. **Say where task logs live** and how to read one for a specific target, since that is the path that actually works.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The repo carries a diagnosis procedure for an unattributed moon failure that is **demonstrated** to surface the cause — proven against a deliberately failing task, with the output recorded.
2. Whether `ciReport.json` can be made to carry stdout/stderr/`exitCode` on moon 2.5.3 is measured and written down, either way.
3. New plans stop reproducing the broken advice; the plan template is the place to fix that.
4. The interaction with `buffer-only-failure` — that a non-reproducing failure's evidence is lost on re-run — is stated wherever the procedure lands.

I read the Linear project and the repo state. Here is what I found.

## Where the MVP milestone stands

Progress is 78%. Target date is 2026-09-30. Two items are in flight, not in the backlog:

- **SMA-579** (Release activation D) — 20 commits on its worktree branch, not merged, with two modified files.
- **SMA-593** (workflow-credentials gate) — open as PR 178.

The MVP backlog holds 15 unstarted issues. Ten of them are CI-machinery work. Two are IAM behaviour. Three are small chores.

## Recommendation: what to do next

**1. Finish the release chain first.** SMA-579 → SMA-580. This is the only epic with a deadline shape, and SMA-580 is the one irreversible step in the repo.

Before you start SMA-580, correct its description. Three checklist items are now stale:

| Checklist item | Actual state |
| --- | --- |
| "`RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` repository secret exists" | Superseded by SMA-589. The workflow mints an App installation token per run. A stored secret cannot work — the token lives one hour. |
| "the repository is public" | Done. `gh repo view` reports `PUBLIC`. |
| "the `release-pr` job has been observed proposing sane versions" | Done. PR 170 (`chore: release v0.1.0`) is open on main. It proposes no version change, which is the expected first-run behaviour the issue predicted. |

**2. Do SMA-596 before SMA-580, not after.** SMA-596 records that `proto` prints NDJSON in an agent session, so `$(proto bin release-plz)` returns a JSON blob and all three `repo:release-parity*` gates abort with rc=2. You cannot locally verify the release gates today. SMA-580 is the irreversible publish step. Fixing the verification path before the irreversible step is the correct order.

**3. Then SMA-588** (twelve Query/Path extractors outside the error envelope). This is the highest-value non-CI item left. It blocks SMA-508 (`@paigasus/sdk`, priority High), because the SDK branches on `(domain, reason)` and a plain-text 400 carries neither. The gate from SMA-587 already reserves the `Query` and `Path` rows with off-flags, so much of the work is a flag flip plus the design decisions.

## Which issues combine

Three merges look sound to me.

**A. SMA-596 + SMA-597 → "make the ci/ tooling's proto and moon calls robust and diagnosable".**
SMA-597's own text proposes this: *"The same tool underlies both … Worth checking whether they share a fix."* SMA-596 is proto's stdout corrupting a caller's parse. SMA-597's measured failure is a proto shim exec error that `ciReport.json` could not surface, found inside `ci/affected-graph/run.sh`'s `moon query` parse — the same family. Both fix `ci/` scripts and both end in a documentation correction. One issue, one review cycle.

**B. SMA-539 + SMA-555 → "lint the CI tooling".**
SMA-539 lints the inline bash in workflows. SMA-555 lints `ci/**/*.py` with ruff. Both add a new `repo:*` gate, so both pay the same ritual: the `T=(…)` array, the CLAUDE.md marker block, the `affected-smoke` re-baseline, `input-liveness`. Paying it once saves real work. SMA-539's own preferred option — extract the long `run:` blocks into `ci/*.sh` — also lands the code in the directory SMA-555's gate covers.

**C. SMA-599 + SMA-552 → "cargo invocation invariants across the Moon graph".**
Both say the same thing about a different invariant. SMA-599: every task running cargo from `rs/` must declare `rs/.cargo/config.toml` as an input (16 of 61 are asserted today). SMA-552: every cargo build should honour `--locked` (one compile gate does). Both need the same derived set — scan each Moon task's command, args and script for a cargo invocation with cwd inside `rs/`. SMA-599 already specifies that derivation with an anti-vacuity floor. Build it once and both checks use it.

One caveat on C: SMA-552 also carries a behavioural change (adding `--locked` to the shared `build` task reds any PR with a stale lock and changes local dev). Merge the derivation work, but keep that flag flip as an explicit decision inside the merged issue.

**Optional ride-along:** SMA-554 (pin `ci.yml`'s `moon ci` lines as exact literals) is a small self-contained refactor of `ci/affected-graph/ci_targets.py`. It can ride with whichever `ci_targets.py` issue lands next rather than get its own cycle.

## What does not combine

- **SMA-600 and SMA-434** look alike and are not. SMA-600 says so directly: the `.pyi` is hand-written, so its drift needs a three-set comparison; the napi glue is generated, so its drift needs regenerate-and-diff. Keep them apart.
- **SMA-588** has its own open design questions (which error reason, a `Path<String>` extractor, whether the gateway reconverges reason 901). Do not fold it into a gate issue.

## Two backlog items to re-read rather than schedule

- **SMA-527** (migrate in-tree deps to path form). Its value dropped after SMA-524 landed the parity gate that asserts `dependsOn` generically. Its measurements are also from Moon 2.3.2, and SMA-595 moved the repo to 2.5.3. Re-measure before you commit to it, or close it.
- **SMA-408** (CLA bot). Priority Low, filed when the repo was private. The repo is public and about to publish to three registries. The priority may deserve a raise.

Want me to apply merges A, B and C in Linear, and correct SMA-580's stale checklist?

# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
name: release

# Only the RELEASE-PR half is live (SMA-576). The release job — tags + registry publishes —
# lands with SMA-580 behind `vars.PAIGASUS_RELEASE_ENABLED`. Nothing here publishes.
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

# release-plz force-updates its PR branch on every run, so two rapid merges to main would
# race. Do NOT cancel in progress: a cancelled run can leave the branch half-written.
concurrency:
  group: release-pr
  cancel-in-progress: false

--- checkout step ---
          # NAME is the only stale thing about it.
          client-id: ${{ secrets.PAIGASUS_BOT_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.PAIGASUS_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          permission-contents: write
          permission-pull-requests: write

        if: steps.preflight.outputs.configured == 'true'
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # persist-credentials: false, matching every other checkout in this repo
          # (artipacked hardening). An earlier revision persisted the App token here so the
          # stamping step could push — but `actions/checkout` writes that credential into
          # the local git config for the WHOLE job, which handed a write-capable token to
          # four steps that have no business with it (setup-toolchain, proto install,
          # moon setup, pnpm install). A compromised action or transitive dependency in any
          # of them could have used it before release work even began.
          #
          # The token now reaches only the two steps that genuinely need it, via their own
          # `env:` — release-plz (GIT_TOKEN) and the stamping step (which authenticates its
          # fetch/push through an explicit remote URL rather than ambient git config).
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up proto + Moon
        if: steps.preflight.outputs.configured == 'true'
        uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095  # v0
        with:
          # Don't cache the proto/Moon toolchain dir: a restored ~/.proto carries stale
          # setup-state that makes `moon setup` skip installing node/pnpm (their shims
          # then don't exist). Reinstall fresh each run (matches ci.yml/prebuild.yml).
          cache: false

      # release-plz is proto-pinned like every other CLI this repo depends on
      # (.prototools, .proto/plugins/release-plz.toml) — install the pinned binary
      # directly rather than through a third-party GitHub Action, which would resolve
      # its own, unpinned release-plz build. Narrow install (not a bare `proto install`):
      # this job needs none of actionlint/buf/deny/machete/nextest/promtool/wasm-pack.
      - name: Install pinned release-plz CLI
        if: steps.preflight.outputs.configured == 'true'
        run: proto install release-plz

      - name: Install Moon-managed toolchains (node, pnpm, rust, python, uv)
        if: steps.preflight.outputs.configured == 'true'
        run: moon setup

      - name: Install JS workspace deps
        if: steps.preflight.outputs.configured == 'true'
        run: pnpm --dir ts install --frozen-lockfile

      # release-plz first, ALWAYS, then --write (next step). release-plz owns every Cargo
      # version and the [workspace.dependencies] requirements; --write then brings the six
      # sites it cannot reach (pyproject/package.json/the dependency pin) plus the three
      # regenerated sites into line.

content.content:
# The ONE place a human approval can be inserted, by adding required reviewers to the
  # `release-approval` environment in repo settings. It must NOT go on the publishing jobs:
  # GitHub pauses EACH job entering an environment, so reviewers on release-publish would stop
  # the run again between crates.io and PyPI — leaving crates.io published and PyPI empty if the
  # second approval is rejected or times out (30 days). That is the split state the job order
  # above exists to prevent. SMA-580: add reviewers HERE, never to release-publish.
  approve-release:
    name: approve the release
    needs: [wheels, prebuild, proto-dist]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: release-approval
    steps:
      - run: echo "Approved. Everything below this point is irreversible."

  release:
    name: publish to crates.io and cut tags
    needs: [wheels, prebuild, proto-dist, approve-release]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    environment: release-publish
    # The irreversible step, serialized. Two merges to main in quick succession would otherwise
    # run two `release-plz release` invocations concurrently, racing the same crates.io publish
    # and the same tag push. NEVER cancel-in-progress here: a cancelled release can leave
    # crates.io half-published with tags partially cut, which is precisely the split state the
    # job ORDER above exists to prevent. A queued second run is safe — release-plz is idempotent
    # and skips packages already published at that version.
    #
    # The build jobs deliberately carry no group: they only produce artifacts, so concurrent
    # runs are harmless, and serializing them would put every push to main behind a full
    # 12-leg matrix.
    concurrency:
      group: release-publish
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      id-token: write    # crates.io OIDC exchange
      contents: read     # the App token below does the writing, not GITHUB_TOKEN
    outputs:
      released: ${{ steps.rel.outputs.json }}
    steps:
      - name: Authenticate with crates.io
        id: cratesio

name: publish to PyPI
    needs: [wheels, proto-dist, release]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    environment: release-publish
    permissions:
      id-token: write    # PyPI trusted publishing; the claim binds to THIS file's name
    steps:
      # `release`'s `released` output is release-plz's own `--output json`, shaped
      # `{"releases":[{"package_name":...,"version":...}]}` (measured against release_plz_core
      # 0.36.14 — "releases"/"package_name", NOT "prs"/"package", which is the OTHER command's
      # shape). paigasus-py-bindings is Cargo `publish = false`, so release-plz never reports
      # it — bind against paigasus-kernel instead, which it definitely reports and which
      # version_group holds to the identical number (repo:version-lockstep asserts that).
      - name: Read the released version
        id: relinfo
          echo "OK: $found wheels at $KERNEL_VERSION"

      # ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: bindings, then the face. skip-existing makes a partial failure
      # re-runnable — PyPI returns 400 "file already exists" otherwise, so an un-skipped retry can
      # never succeed unaided. PyPI is delete-but-never-reuse.
      - name: Publish paigasus-py-bindings
        if: steps.relinfo.outputs.kernel_release == 'true'
        uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@dc37677b2e1c63e2034f94d8a5b11f265b73ba33  # v1.14.2
        with:
          packages-dir: dist-bindings
          skip-existing: true

      - name: Publish paigasus-kernel
        if: steps.relinfo.outputs.kernel_release == 'true'
        uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@dc37677b2e1c63e2034f94d8a5b11f265b73ba33  # v1.14.2
        with:
          packages-dir: dist-face
          skip-existing: true

      # Independent cadence: release-plz sees the RUST crate `paigasus-proto`; what uploads here
      # is the PYTHON distribution built from py/packages/paigasus-proto. Same name, two things.
      - name: Publish paigasus-proto
        if: steps.relinfo.outputs.proto_release == 'true'
        uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@dc37677b2e1c63e2034f94d8a5b11f265b73ba33  # v1.14.2
        with:
          packages-dir: dist-proto
          skip-existing: true

  publish-npm:
    name: publish to npm
